subject: Elara Health — post-demo costing playbook & invoice sketch
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Elara Health — post-demo costing playbook & invoice sketch

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for your time on the demo earlier — appreciated the clarity on the two pilot flows (Clinical Notes ingestion + patient Q&A widget). Per our ask, I captured a short costing playbook and attached a first-pass invoice sketch and spreadsheet that show the sensitivity to token mix, sequence length, and batching.

Recap of what we scoped:
- Pilot duration: 3 months (starting Dec 1)
- Estimated daily active users: 1,200 (peak 2,500)
- Average session: ~120 user tokens in + 140 model tokens out (prefill + response)
- Expected tokens/day (baseline): ~312k user + 364k model = ~676k tokens/day (~20M tokens/month)

Cost/price guidance (high level summary in sheet):
- Unit target: Elara indicated a target contribution around $500 per 1M tokens for hosted inference in pilot (you mentioned a range of $400–$650). We built estimates at $350, $500, and $650 / 1M tokens to reflect different batching/quantization outcomes.
- For 20M tokens/mo this maps to a hosted invoice range of roughly $7k — $13k depending on config (see tab: "unit-scenarios").

Key levers we called out in the attachment:
1) Model variant: smaller quantized variant reduces token cost by ~25–40% for same output quality in this workload.
2) Batch/latency tradeoff: small batching for interactive widget keeps p99 sub-300ms but increases per-token unit cost by ~10–20%.
3) Prefix/KV caching: clinical notes reuse will save ~8–12% of model tokens if we enable aggressive KV caching.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm whether the pilot includes patient PII (will change deployment & compliance needs).
2) If pilot allowed to run on Redwood Hosted we’ll send a formal invoice sketch for the first month and a Dedicated commitment option (3-month commit) for a lower unit price.
3) If procurement wants an itemized line (SaaS + tokens + storage + support), we’ll add that to the PDF.

Attachments: pricing workbook (redwood-pricing-playbook-v1.xlsx), invoice sketch (elara-invoice-sketch.pdf).

Quick ask: can you share the expected sample session traces (anonymized) or average sequence lengths per flow? That will let us lock the numbers to within ~10%.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Marissa on a Dedicated vs Hosted delta and a clean invoice ready for procurement.

—
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Elara Health — post-demo costing playbook & invoice sketch

Jonas — thanks for the thoughtful breakdown and for sending the workbook. A few quick clarifications from procurement and product: 

- Pilot will include de-identified clinical notes (we will confirm exact de-id process; likely meets HIPAA BA requirements but we need documentation).
- The $400–$650 / 1M tokens range is what leadership gave as a comfortable per-unit cost; product would prefer to target the lower half if we do Hosted.
- Our initial budget for the pilot is $40k total over 3 months but we may stretch to $60k if quality and latency meet SLAs.

Questions: 
1) What does the Hosted invoice number look like after we enable KV caching aggressively?
2) If we commit to a 3-month Dedicated pool (guaranteed capacity) what is the target $/1M token you can offer for 20M tokens/mo?

Looping in procurement on cc — procurement will want a simple line-item invoice and evidence of SOC2 + data retention policies.

—Samira

Jonas / Karthik — forwarding Samira's note. Two quick internal points: 

- If they can commit to 20M tokens/mo and a 3-month Dedicated commit, we can go to $300 / 1M tokens effective unit (requires committed capacity + standard enterprise support). This assumes they accept a quantized model variant and maintain p95 latency <500ms.
- Hosted (no commit) aggressive caching scenario: we estimate effective unit at ~$420 / 1M tokens after KV caching and medium batching (table in the workbook). That would put a 3-month pilot at ~20M tokens/mo * $420 * 3 = $25,200. With their $40k budget that leaves headroom for growth and extra support lines.

Action items:
- Jonas: prepare two invoice options for Samira — (A) Hosted pilot month-by-month with caching enabled (line items + example invoice PDF), (B) Dedicated 3-month commit with unit price and uplift for enterprise support. Include SOC2 attestation link.
- Karthik: please add a Dedicated commitment row in the pricing workbook (tab: "committed-offers") with GPU config and expected throughput/latency numbers.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Elara Health — post-demo costing playbook & invoice sketch

Samira — quick follow with the two invoice options attached and a short note on unit math. Please find: redwood-pricing-playbook-v1.xlsx and elara-invoice-sketch.pdf. Highlights: 

Option A — Hosted (monthly, no commit)- Baseline tokens: 20M/mo- Unit scenarios: $350 / 1M (aggressive quant + high batch), $420 / 1M (aggressive KV caching + balanced batch), $650 / 1M (low batching, full-precision)- Example invoice (month 1): $7,000 — $13,000

Option B — Dedicated commit (3 months)- Committed tokens: 20M/mo guaranteed throughput- Offered unit: $300 / 1M tokens (requires quantized model & standard enterprise support)- 3-month committed invoice: $18,000 (tokens) + $4,500 monthly reserved capacity = $22,500 / month; total commitment $67,500 over 3 months.

Notes on assumptions:
- We assumed 45% model token vs user token split in the workbook. If your session mix has longer model responses, math shifts proportionally.
- SOC2: https://redwood.com/security/soc2-attestation (link included in invoice cover).

Next recommended step: procurement signs the pilot SOW (we’ll put the Hosted vs Dedicated options in an SOW appendix) and we run a short one-week pre-production profiling job against a 10k-session sample. That will reduce the unit estimate variance to ±8%.

If procurement approves, I’ll drop a DocuSign SOW and an itemized invoice for month 1.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
